wiki.unwritten_rule: When selecting clearing houses for London exchange trades, Enron staff rely on informal back-office quality assessments, favoring Bank Paribas over Carr based on past experience.
wiki.applies_when: Choosing clearing houses for London exchange transactions, especially when multiple options are available.
wiki.exceptions: Unknown; may differ if counterparty or regulatory requirements dictate a specific clearer.
wiki.alternative: Selection might be driven by formal vendor assessments or contractual obligations rather than personal experience.
wiki.uncertainty: Single episode; no evidence of repeated pattern or official policy.
wiki.next_query: Look for other emails discussing clearing house selection or preferences to see if Paribas is consistently favored.
wiki.inference_gap: Sources do not explicitly state a policy or preference; Maria's opinion is personal and based on past dealings. The contrast between Mark's neutral statement and Maria's evaluative reply suggests an informal knowledge hierarchy, but this is not confirmed.
wiki.evidence_basis: Two separate emails in the same thread: Mark Elliott's message to Maria Nartey and Maria's reply. Both are authored by different actors in the same episode, discussing OMLX clearing arrangements.
wiki.prediction: Future communications about London clearing will likely reference Paribas as the preferred clearer, unless specific circumstances dictate otherwise.

evidence.quote:
Maria,

The Clearing docs we got in from the Exchange showed Merrill Lynch in London 
as Houston's clearer.  This is not to say this is fixed, but for some reason 
the OMLX were under the impression that it would be Merrills.  By the way, we 
can have as many clearers as we like (provided, of course, that they are 
General Clearing Members at the OMLX).

If you could let me now quite swiftly on this issue I would be very grateful 
as we finalised the legal points on Clearing docs a couple of weeks ago and I 
have already couriered the final  versions for signature to Houston. 

Kind regards

Mark

evidence.quote:
Dayton Power is away from the office on Friday and Monday for the new year
holiday.  They have requested nominations for the 1st to the 4th by 2:00 
today.

The first day of January is the most critical.  I will have the ability to
adjust any of the days from my home over the weekend on an intraday basis.

I will need to work with Joann and Joni (Tco schedulers) to get the 
nominations
in place.

I'll call you, Chris, after morning trading to devise a game plan for the 1st.

If Joann works here today, I'm going to need to stay close by.

sg
evidence.claim: Schedulers coordinate nominations for holiday periods via phone and intraday adjustments from home, indicating flexible off-hours work.
